messages:
ian_sales: @alice_customer quick one — for the POC you mentioned private connectivity across 3 AWS accounts, do you want PrivateLink per-account or a shared peering approach?
alice_customer: We prefer not to open peering due to blast radius. Leaning PrivateLink. Need static egress IPs so our firewall can allowlist callbacks. Any gotchas?
julie_netops: PrivateLink is good for no-routing-change isolation. Note: PrivateLink endpoints are regional and you need an NLB on our side to front the service.
matt_eng: For static egress IPs: if callbacks go to the internet from your VPC, you control static EIP via NAT Gateway. If callbacks are to customer systems inside VPC, traffic should stay internal and no egress IP required.
sarah_se: Quick cost note for the customer: PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint charges + per-GB data processing on AWS; we also bill for Private deployments licensing and egress traffic if using public internet paths. I'll follow up with a line-item estimate.
alice_customer: For the POC we want minimal infra changes. Can we do PrivateLink + NAT EIP so we have 1 allowlisted IP for callbacks to our on-prem firewall?
julie_netops: Yes — pattern: create PrivateLink endpoint for inbound calls to Redwood service, and route outbound callbacks through a NAT Gateway with Elastic IP. Remember security groups on the endpoint ENIs must allow the customer subnets.
matt_eng: Also watch healthchecks: our side will open connections on port 443. Primary is 443 TLS. If you need mutual TLS we can swap certs.
ian_sales: Action items: julie to add firewall snippet, matt to confirm ports and TLS/mTLS support, sarah to add cost blurb. target: POC kickoff tomorrow.
julie_netops: Firewall snippet for customers (example, egress rules to allow callbacks via NAT EIP):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood callbacks (via NAT EIP 203.0.113.45)
# Outbound: TCP 443 to 203.0.113.45/32
# Allow PrivateLink ENIs (example, replace with actual ENI IPs)
# Inbound from ENI range: TCP 443
```
julie_netops: Also ensure SGs allow ephemeral return ports (TCP 1024-65535) for established connections if using stateful firewalls.
matt_eng: For multi-account: we can create one PrivateLink per account, or expose a single endpoint service in our account and customers create endpoints in theirs. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can also deploy per-customer NLBs.
sarah_se: Pricing estimate: PrivateLink addon + per-GB egress. I'll DM a sample calc.
alice_customer: Okay that's helpful. One more: if we can't use PrivateLink in one account for policy reasons, can we fall back to VPC peering for that account only?
matt_eng: Yes fallback works. We support routing policies — we'll route the traffic via peering for that account. Note peering can add transitive limitations; TGW could be an alternative.
ian_sales: Great. Thanks all. I'll schedule the kickoff and share updated checklist. :thumbsup:
